F1.name: immediate_o_to_s
F1.description: The opening decision corrects immediately from O to S before browser work; medium and hard tasks may continue with causally required downstream operations.

F2.name: search_attempt_then_o
F2.description: The opening decision makes a bounded good-faith S attempt, then falls back to O only after structural insufficiency is established.

F3.name: causal_s_to_o
F3.description: The opening decision uses S to produce an entity, constraint, identifier, threshold, or shortlist required by O.

F4.name: causal_o_to_s
F4.description: The opening decision uses O to surface an entity, offer, item, metric, artifact, or status that binds the subsequent S question.

standard.attempt_rigor: two materially different exact-query formulations plus one relevant result inspection

easy.attempt_rigor: one exact query plus one relevant result inspection

medium.attempt_rigor: two materially different query formulations plus one authoritative result inspection

hard.attempt_rigor: decompose the exact request into at least three search angles and establish that no indexed source exposes the required combined state

search_prototypes.name: Organization identity and background
search_prototypes.goal: establish who operates the relevant site or entity, where it is based, and the key dated background fact needed by the user

search_prototypes.name: Entity identification by public constraints
search_prototypes.goal: identify the named entity that satisfies the public, stable constraints in the scenario

search_prototypes.name: Public candidate shortlist
search_prototypes.goal: build a short candidate set satisfying stable public criteria before live comparison

search_prototypes.name: Resolve a relevant location
search_prototypes.goal: identify the location, hub, venue, district, or waypoint that best satisfies the stated geographic constraint

search_prototypes.name: Resolve an official date window
search_prototypes.goal: determine the authoritative event, season, deadline, or eligibility dates needed to parameterize the live task

search_prototypes.name: Derive requirement set
search_prototypes.goal: derive the stable policy, technical, accessibility, dietary, or eligibility requirements that the live result must satisfy

search_prototypes.name: Resolve public identifier
search_prototypes.goal: resolve the canonical identifier, ticker, filing number, model code, station code, or standardized name needed for an exact lookup

search_prototypes.name: Find a decision threshold
search_prototypes.goal: find the authoritative benchmark, limit, target, or recommended threshold to apply in the interactive tool

search_prototypes.name: Resolve classification
search_prototypes.goal: determine the official category, risk class, genre, role family, or product class needed to choose the correct interface controls

search_prototypes.name: Official policy or eligibility check
search_prototypes.goal: use the surfaced entity or result to determine the applicable official policy, eligibility rule, restriction, or obligation

search_prototypes.name: External benchmark comparison
search_prototypes.goal: compare the surfaced price, quote, metric, route, or calculated value with an authoritative public benchmark on the same basis

search_prototypes.name: Creator, owner, or operator lookup
search_prototypes.goal: identify the creator, owner, operator, manufacturer, or issuing authority behind the surfaced item

search_prototypes.name: Independent reputation comparison
search_prototypes.goal: use independent public sources to compare reputation, reviews, awards, or reliability for the surfaced option or shortlist

search_prototypes.name: Historical context
search_prototypes.goal: place the surfaced entity, metric, status, or result in the relevant historical sequence or prior-period context

search_prototypes.name: Technical compatibility verification
search_prototypes.goal: verify from authoritative documentation whether the surfaced configuration, artifact, build, or item is compatible with the user's external system or requirement

search_prototypes.name: Safety and accessibility follow-up
search_prototypes.goal: determine the relevant safety, accessibility, health, or operational constraints for the surfaced route, venue, service, or plan

search_prototypes.name: Public alternative discovery
search_prototypes.goal: find a publicly documented alternative when the surfaced live result is unavailable, over budget, incompatible, or otherwise unsuitable

search_prototypes.name: Method, definition, and unit verification
search_prototypes.goal: verify the public definition, method, units, coverage, and limitations needed to interpret the surfaced metric or computed result

search_prototypes.name: Official specification lookup
search_prototypes.goal: retrieve the authoritative specifications and limits for the surfaced product, asset, record, or output

search_prototypes.name: Multi-source enrichment join
search_prototypes.goal: join the surfaced entities with the same public attributes from multiple sources and return a comparable table

search_prototypes.name: Conjunctive entity identification
search_prototypes.goal: identify an initially unknown entity that uniquely satisfies at least four independent clues distributed across multiple sources
entity_space: unknown person, place, organization, product, work, or event
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Identify the unknown entity satisfying all stated clues, verify each clue, and use the resolved name as the downstream input.

search_prototypes.name: Exhaustive constrained shortlist
search_prototypes.goal: enumerate a candidate universe, intersect several independently sourced constraints, deduplicate aliases, and return the complete qualifying shortlist
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Find all candidates satisfying the stated cross-source constraints and justify why the shortlist is complete.

search_prototypes.name: Cross-source location resolution
search_prototypes.goal: resolve the exact location that best satisfies geographic, jurisdictional, schedule, accessibility, and proximity constraints drawn from multiple sources
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Determine which exact location satisfies all geographic and operational constraints, then use its canonical place name or code downstream.

search_prototypes.name: Temporal provenance and date-window derivation
search_prototypes.goal: reconstruct a dated sequence across authoritative records and derive the exact future window in which all eligibility, event, season, or policy constraints overlap
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Reconcile the relevant dated records and derive the exact date window that can be used in the downstream live query.

search_prototypes.name: Multi-authority requirement synthesis
search_prototypes.goal: combine policy, technical, legal, accessibility, or compatibility requirements from several authorities into one operational constraint set
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Synthesize the authoritative requirements into a concrete set of controls or filters for the downstream operation.

search_prototypes.name: Canonical identifier relationship chain
search_prototypes.goal: follow a multi-hop relationship chain to resolve the canonical code, registry ID, ticker, model number, station code, or normalized name required for an exact lookup
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Traverse the named relationships and registries to resolve the exact canonical identifier required downstream.

search_prototypes.name: Normalized multi-source threshold
search_prototypes.goal: collect comparable numeric evidence from multiple sources, normalize units and time bases, calculate the requested benchmark, and return the decision threshold
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Collect and normalize the required figures, show the calculation, and use the resulting threshold in the downstream operation.

search_prototypes.name: Cross-authority classification reconciliation
search_prototypes.goal: reconcile conflicting taxonomies, definitions, editions, or jurisdictions and determine the one classification applicable to the user's scenario
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Compare the relevant classification systems and resolve which exact class applies before choosing downstream controls.

search_prototypes.name: Deep result enrichment table
search_prototypes.goal: take every entity surfaced by the operation, resolve stable join keys, collect the same public attributes from multiple sources, and produce a comparable qualified table
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: For every surfaced entity, join the requested public attributes from independent sources and return a comparable table.

search_prototypes.name: Conflicting-source result reconciliation
search_prototypes.goal: use the surfaced entity or value to gather conflicting public claims, compare definitions, dates, scope, units, and authority, and resolve which interpretation applies
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Investigate conflicting public claims about the surfaced result and resolve them under an explicit authority and scope rule.

search_prototypes.name: Historical provenance of surfaced result
search_prototypes.goal: trace the surfaced entity, item, status, or metric through a dated origin, ownership, release, renaming, or prior-period chain and explain the verified transitions
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Use the surfaced identity to reconstruct its relevant dated provenance chain from origin to the requested endpoint.

search_prototypes.name: Scholarly or technical evidence synthesis
search_prototypes.goal: formulate a focused question from the surfaced result, locate multiple primary or review sources, and synthesize methods, findings, disagreement, and limitations
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Use the surfaced result to bind a focused evidence question and synthesize agreement, disagreement, methods, and limitations across sources.

search_prototypes.name: Cross-site result-to-constraint bridge
search_prototypes.goal: use the exact result surfaced on one site to look up the policy, compatibility, eligibility, or comparison rule that becomes a concrete constraint for the next site's operation
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Use the first site's exact result to derive the constraint needed to configure the next site.

search_prototypes.name: Cross-site canonical-identifier bridge
search_prototypes.goal: resolve the surfaced result to the canonical name, code, model, listing identity, or normalized join key required for an exact operation on the next site
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Normalize the first site's result to the exact identifier accepted by the next site.

search_prototypes.name: Deep cross-site requirement reconciliation
search_prototypes.goal: take the prior site's exact result, reconcile multi-source policy, technical, legal, or compatibility requirements, and produce one operational constraint set for the next site
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Reconcile the authoritative requirements attached to the surfaced result and convert them into exact controls for the next operation.

search_prototypes.name: Deep cross-site candidate transfer
search_prototypes.goal: expand and verify the exact entity surfaced on one site against several public sources, reconcile aliases and exclusions, and produce a qualified candidate set for the next site's operation
search_prototypes.question_skeleton: Use the surfaced entity to build a verified candidate set that can be tested on the next site.
